slice: rmcp-v3.1.4 exact task parameter and acknowledgement dispatch shapes
exact_findings: GetTaskParams has meta: Option<RequestMetaObject> and task_id: String; GetTaskParams::new(task_id) sets meta=None and stores task_id.
CancelTaskParams has meta: Option<RequestMetaObject> and task_id: String; CancelTaskParams::new(task_id) sets meta=None and stores task_id.
UpdateTaskParams has meta: Option<RequestMetaObject>, task_id: String, and input_responses: InputResponses; its constructor accepts task_id plus InputResponses.
ServerResult contains TaskAckResult after CallToolResult/InputRequiredResult in the untagged union, and ServerResult::task_ack(()) wraps TaskAckResult::new().

The exact ServerHandler dispatcher validates Tasks capability before tasks/* handlers. tasks/get calls get_task(params, context) and maps GetTaskResult directly; tasks/update and tasks/cancel call update_task/cancel_task and map successful () through ServerResult::task_ack.

Therefore an application-owned task store can key get/update/cancel lookup directly by the server-stable task_id carried in the typed params while preserving the stock dispatcher acknowledgement wire shape, without requiring those three handlers to return a stock TaskManager-specific type.
scope_limits: This slice does not prove restart execution/redrive, create-or-get idempotency, effect exactly-once semantics, or authorization of task_id ownership.
It does not compile a custom persistent ServerHandler implementation.
It does not prove that stock TaskManager is replaceable internally; it only pins the public ServerHandler parameter/result seam for application-owned implementations.
Current-main search was used only to locate model.rs; substantive claims above were re-fetched from the exact release commit.
